title: Randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, parallel-group, prospective clinical study to analyse the effects of vicadrostat and empagliflozin on blood pressure and vascular structure and function in patients with uncontrolled arterial hypertension
official: Randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, parallel-group, prospective clinical study to analyse the effects of vicadrostat and empagliflozin on blood pressure and vascular structure and function in patients with uncontrolled arterial hypertension
summary: Main objective: To prove the hypothesis that vicadrostat/empagliflozin is able to reduce office systolic BP in patients with uncontrolled arterial hypertension after 12 weeks of treatment
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age at screening ≥ 18 years but <80 years for male and female patients
2. Uncontrolled arterial hypertension defined according to office BP measurements and current guidelines (mean systolic ≥ 140 mmHg and/or mean diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg) AND mean systolic 24-hour ambulatory BP ≥ 130 and/or mean diastolic 24-hour ambulatory BP ≥ 80 mmHg
3. Uncontrolled hypertension with 1-3 antihypertensive drug classes (stable dose of at least 4 weeks before screening; renin angiotensin system blockade is mandatory)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Has the following known secondary causes of hypertension: severe renal artery stenosis, uncontrolled or untreated hyperthyroidism, uncontrolled or untreated hypothyroidism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing’s syndrome, primary hyperaldosteronism, aortic coarctation
2. Hepatic cirrhosis (Child–Pugh C)
3. Significant abnormality of ALT and/or AST (>3x ULN)
4. Any history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, instable angina pectoris, or myocardial infarction within the last 6 months prior to study inclusion
5. Individuals at risk for poor protocol or medication compliance
6. Patients in unstable conditions due to any kind of serious disease, that interferes with the conduct of the trial
7. Female who is pregnant, breast feeding or intends to become pregnant. Documentation of highly effective contraception is required for women of childbearing potential (WOCBP). A WOCBP, i.e. fertile, following menarche and until becoming post-menopausal unless permanently sterile
8. Potassium of ≥5.2 mmol/l
9. Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR; Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration [CKD-EPI] formula) < 20 ml/min/1.73m² and/or UACR ≥ 3500 mg/g in spot urine
10. Office BP repeatedly ≥ 180/110 mmHg
11. Treatment with inhibitors of aldosterone-mediated effects (e.g., MRAs, ASI, renin inhibitor) or potassium-sparing diuretics within the past 12 weeks
12. Congestive heart failure (CHF) NYHA stage III and IV
13. Systemic mineralocorticoid replacement therapy (e.g. fludrocortisone)
14. Known adrenal insufficiency (e.g. Addison disease)
15. Intolerance/known allergy/hypersensitivity to vicadrostat, empagliflozin, other SGLT2i, and/or excipients (incl. lactose)
16. Combination treatment of ACEi and an ARB or ACEi/ARB with ARNI within the past 12 weeks
17. HbA1c ≥ 10.0%
18. Major surgery planned during the trial
19. Enrolment in another investigational device or drug trial ≤30 days since ending or within 5x half-lives of last unlicensed IMP dose (whichever is longer)
20. Chronic alcohol or drug abuse
21. Active malignancy at screening, confirmed malignancy or treatment for cancer within ≤2 years of screening except localized non-melanoma skin cancer or low- grade cancers (e.g. intraepithelial neoplasia)
22. T1DM or diabetes of other autoimmune causes
23. SGLT2 inhibitor therapy or insulin therapy within the last 3 months
24. History of severe orthostatic dysregulation
